items.title: Heavy Snow Disrupts Austria
items.gist: A powerful snowfall blanketed much of the country, including Vienna. Roads and transport faced a difficult day.
items.summary: Heavy snow fell across many parts of Austria on Thursday. Vienna recorded 17 centimetres at Hohe Warte, the most November snow there in more than 40 years. The A21 motorway was closed for several hours after vehicles became stuck. Accidents and delays were also reported in other regions. Forecasters said cold weather could keep the snow on the ground into next week.
items.host_open: Vienna got a very wintry November surprise. How does that look from Austria?

items.title: Nehammer Denies Media Pressure
items.gist: Former chancellor Karl Nehammer answered questions in a parliamentary inquiry. The hearing focused on claims linked to a secret recording.
items.summary: Former Austrian chancellor Karl Nehammer appeared before a parliamentary inquiry on Thursday. The inquiry concerns Christian Pilnacek, a former senior justice official who died in 2023. A recording of Pilnacek had included claims of political pressure on investigations. Nehammer denied trying to influence the ORF or the newspaper Kronen Zeitung. He said he spoke to the newspaper's editor only after hearing a witness's claim. The inquiry is examining what happened and who knew about it.
items.host_open: A parliamentary hearing can bring old questions back into the room. What did you make of Nehammer’s answer?

items.title: Vienna Cuts Culture Spending
items.gist: Vienna plans to save €31 million from its cultural budget. Some major venues and festivals say the cuts leave little time to adjust.
items.summary: Vienna's culture department must save €31 million in its 2027 budget. The cuts affect theatres, festivals and other cultural institutions. The city plans to end the Kultursommer and pause the Klima Biennale. Some theatres have criticised both the size of the cuts and the short notice. The city says it must reduce spending because of financial pressure. It says some cultural support and free entry at the Wien Museum will continue.
items.host_open: Vienna’s cultural calendar may soon have fewer events. How do you feel about that?

items.title: Ukraine Warns of Power Grid Attack
items.gist: Ukraine's president says Russia may be preparing a major strike on energy systems. Kyiv is asking partners for more air defence equipment.
items.summary: President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Russia may launch a major attack on Ukraine's energy infrastructure. He warned that logistics and other critical services could also be targeted. Russian missile and drone attacks have damaged Ukraine's power system during the war. Ukraine says it needs more air defence supplies, including Patriot interceptors. The United States envoy said Russian President Vladimir Putin had shown restraint by agreeing not to use nuclear weapons. Russia's latest attack plans were not independently confirmed.
items.host_open: Winter power is vital for people across Ukraine. How do you feel about the warning?

items.title: New Strikes Reported in Gaza
items.gist: Israeli strikes and gunfire killed people in Gaza, according to local authorities. The reports come amid continuing violence despite a ceasefire deal.
items.summary: Israeli strikes and gunfire killed 10 people in Gaza, according to Palestinian health authorities. Israel said it had targeted Hamas figures and military sites. The deaths are part of continuing violence more than a year after a ceasefire deal was reached. Hamas and Israel have offered different accounts of responsibility for the fighting. The Associated Press said it could not independently verify some claims in its report. Civilians in Gaza remain at risk as the exchanges continue.
items.host_open: Another night of strikes has brought more loss to Gaza. How does this news make you feel?

items.title: Ebola Cases Rise in Eastern Congo
items.gist: The outbreak has passed 12,000 confirmed cases, official data says. Fighting is making it harder for health teams to respond.
items.summary: Congo's health ministry reported more than 12,000 confirmed Ebola cases on Thursday. The outbreak is spreading in the country's east. Fighting between armed groups and government forces has disrupted efforts to contain the virus. Some response teams have had to leave areas because of security risks. Health workers are trying to find cases and limit further spread. The situation matters beyond the region because outbreaks can cross borders.
items.host_open: Health teams are working under difficult and unsafe conditions. How do you feel about their challenge?

items.title: EU Leaders Debate Budget and Ukraine Aid
items.gist: Leaders met in Brussels to discuss the bloc’s next long-term budget. They also face a difficult question: how to cover Ukraine’s needs in 2027.
items.summary: European Union leaders met in Brussels on Thursday and Friday. They discussed the EU budget for 2028 to 2034 and funding for Ukraine in 2027. The budget proposal is worth nearly €1.6 trillion. Member states disagree about its size and how money should be shared. Some governments want tighter spending, while others argue for more support for regions and Ukraine. Leaders are trying to narrow differences ahead of a planned decision in December.
items.host_open: Brussels has a very large bill to divide. How do you see the debate?

items.title: Spain’s De Cos Chosen for ECB Role
items.gist: EU leaders selected Spain’s former central bank chief to lead the European Central Bank. Inflation and borrowing costs will be major challenges for the incoming president.
items.summary: EU leaders chose Pablo Hernández de Cos to become the next president of the European Central Bank. He previously led Spain's central bank. He is set to succeed Christine Lagarde, who is leaving before the end of her term. The ECB sets monetary policy for countries that use the euro. Leaders face concerns about inflation, government debt and borrowing costs. De Cos will need to guide the bank through those pressures.
items.host_open: The next ECB chief will inherit a demanding job. What do you think will matter most?

items.title: Serbia Calls Early Presidential Vote
items.gist: Serbia will hold a presidential election on December 27. The vote follows a parliamentary result that reshaped the political landscape.
items.summary: Serbia's parliament speaker called a presidential election for December 27. Former president Aleksandar Vučić resigned in September to try to become prime minister. That attempt failed. A student-led list won the most seats in October's parliamentary election. The new presidential vote will test how that result changes national politics. The authorities say voters should take part and choose a president with strong public support.
items.host_open: Serbia has a new election date and a changed political balance. Did that surprise you?

items.title: Thanksgiving Storm Delays Parade
items.gist: Bad weather forced New York to postpone its famous Thanksgiving parade. Flooding and power cuts affected other parts of the United States too.
items.summary: Severe weather disrupted Thanksgiving celebrations across the United States. New York postponed the Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade for the first time in its history. Heavy rain and strong winds caused flooding in parts of the East Coast. Snow and power outages were also reported elsewhere. Organisers faced the problem of rearranging performances and travel plans. Officials urged people to follow local weather and safety advice.
items.host_open: Even the parade had to change its plans this year. Did that surprise you?

items.title: Markets Rise as US Takes Holiday
items.gist: European and Asian shares moved higher while US markets were closed for Thanksgiving. Investors are still watching technology stocks closely.
items.summary: Shares rose in European and Asian markets on Thursday. US stock markets were closed for the Thanksgiving holiday. Investors were responding to a recent rebound in technology shares. Concerns about high valuations in artificial intelligence companies have unsettled markets this month. The latest move offered some relief but does not settle those concerns. Traders will watch how US markets react when they reopen.
items.host_open: Investors got a holiday pause in the United States, but markets elsewhere kept moving. How do you read the rebound?

items.title: Free Books Fill Bologna Street
items.gist: A bookshop owner put nearly 10,000 books outside for people to take. The giveaway helped the shop avoid throwing them away before moving nearby.
items.summary: A bookshop in Bologna gave away nearly 10,000 books before moving to a new location. Owner Davide Scilabra placed the books outside for free collection. The books covered subjects including art, languages, philosophy and mathematics. He said he wanted to keep them from being thrown away. The giveaway attracted readers and students. Almost all the books had been taken by Thursday, according to reports cited by ORF.
items.host_open: A bookshop turned moving day into a gift for readers. What kind of book would you have picked?

items.title: Vienna Opera Honours Welser-Möst
items.gist: The Vienna State Opera named conductor Franz Welser-Möst an honorary member. The award recognises his long connection with the house.
items.summary: The Vienna State Opera made conductor Franz Welser-Möst an honorary member. The ceremony took place after a performance of Ariadne auf Naxos. He first conducted at the opera house in 1987. He later served as its general music director from 2010 to 2014. The opera described honorary membership as its highest award. Welser-Möst called the house an important artistic home for him.
items.host_open: A long musical partnership has earned a special honour. How does that feel as a cultural story from Vienna?

items.title: Italy Expands Nuclear Defence Spending
items.gist: Britain plans to spend billions on nuclear deterrence, according to Austrian public radio’s evening news list. The decision raises questions about security and public spending.
items.summary: Britain is planning billions of pounds in spending on nuclear deterrence, according to an item in ORF's evening news rundown. The report described the plans as part of the country's defence policy. Nuclear deterrence aims to discourage an attack by threatening a response. Supporters say the capability is needed in a more dangerous security environment. Critics often question its cost and risks. The available report summary did not give further details about the spending plan.
items.host_open: Nuclear deterrence brings security and cost questions together. How do you feel about that balance?
